    DevelopBranch --> DevDeploy: Auto-Deploy Triggered<br/>(GitHub Actions)
    
    DevDeploy --> DevTesting: Deployment Complete<br/>(2-4 containers)
    
    DevTesting --> MainBranch: Tests Pass<br/>Merge to Main
    
    MainBranch --> StagingDeploy: Auto-Deploy Triggered<br/>(GitHub Actions)
    
    StagingDeploy --> StagingValidation: Deployment Complete<br/>(2-6 containers)
    
    StagingValidation --> ProductionApproval: Validation Successful<br/>(Integration tests pass)
    
    ProductionApproval --> ProductionDeploy: Manual Approval<br/>(Engineering Manager)
    
    ProductionDeploy --> ProductionMonitoring: Rolling Deployment<br/>(Zero downtime)
    
    ProductionMonitoring --> ProductionSuccess: No Issues Detected<br/>(30-minute observation)
    
    ProductionMonitoring --> ProductionRollback: Issues Detected<br/>(High error rate, latency)
    
    ProductionRollback --> ProductionApproval: Fix and Re-Deploy
    
    ProductionSuccess --> [*]: Release Complete
    
    note right of FeatureBranch
        Branch: feature/xyz
        CI: Run tests on push
        No deployment
    end note
    
    note right of DevDeploy
        Environment: Development
        Trigger: Automatic
        Containers: 2-4
        Database: M10 tier

    end note
    
    note right of StagingDeploy
        Environment: Staging
        Trigger: Automatic
        Containers: 2-6
        Database: M20 tier
        Users: QA team, beta testers
    end note
    
    note right of ProductionDeploy
        Environment: Production

**Deployment Workflow Details**:

**Development Environment**:
- **Trigger**: Automatic on merge to `develop` branch
- **Purpose**: Validate feature functionality in cloud environment
- **Deployment Time**: 5-10 minutes
- **Rollback**: Revert merge to `develop` branch, redeploy
- **Monitoring**: Basic CloudWatch logs, manual testing by developers

**Staging Environment**:
- **Trigger**: Automatic on merge to `main` branch
- **Purpose**: Integration testing, QA validation, performance testing
- **Deployment Time**: 5-10 minutes
- **Rollback**: Revert merge to `main` branch, redeploy
- **Validation**: Automated integration tests, manual QA testing
- **Data**: Sanitized production data (PII masked) or synthetic test data

**Production Environment**:
- **Trigger**: Manual approval after staging validation
- **Approval Required**: Engineering Manager or designated approver
- **Pre-Deployment Checklist**:
  - All tests passing in staging
  - Code review completed
  - Release notes drafted
  - Database migrations tested (if applicable)
  - Monitoring alerts reviewed and adjusted
  - On-call engineer notified
- **Deployment Time**: 10-15 minutes (rolling update)
- **Rollback**: Update to previous task definition (5-10 minutes)
- **Monitoring**: 30-minute observation window post-deployment

**Promotion Criteria**:

| From Environment | To Environment | Required Checks |
|-----------------|----------------|-----------------|
| Feature Branch → Development | All unit tests pass, code linting passes, security scan passes (no CRITICAL vulnerabilities) |
| Development → Staging | Feature validation complete, no known blockers, merge to `main` branch |
| Staging → Production | Integration tests pass, QA approval, no P0/P1 bugs, manual approval obtained, 24-hour soak test in staging |

#### 8.2.2.4 Backup and Disaster Recovery Plans

**MongoDB Atlas Continuous Backup**:

**Backup Schedule**:
- **Snapshot Frequency**: 
  - Daily snapshots: Retained for 7 days
  - Weekly snapshots: Retained for 4 weeks
  - Monthly snapshots: Retained for 12 months
- **Point-in-Time Recovery**: 1-minute granularity, 24-hour retention window
- **Backup Storage**: Encrypted backups stored in MongoDB Atlas infrastructure with cross-region replication
- **Cross-Region Replication**: Automated backup replication to DR region (us-west-2)

**Backup Configuration by Environment**:

| Environment | Snapshot Retention | Point-in-Time Recovery | Cross-Region Backup |
|-------------|-------------------|------------------------|---------------------|
| **Development** | 2 days | Disabled | No |
| **Staging** | 7 days | 24 hours | No |
| **Production** | Daily: 7d, Weekly: 4w, Monthly: 12m | 24 hours | Yes (us-west-2) |

**Backup Restoration Procedures**:

**Scenario 1: Data Corruption (Recent)**
- **Trigger**: Application bug causes data corruption detected within 24 hours
- **Recovery Method**: Point-in-time restore to timestamp before corruption
- **RTO (Recovery Time Objective)**: < 2 hours
- **RPO (Recovery Point Objective)**: < 1 minute
- **Process**:
  1. Identify corruption timestamp from audit logs
  2. Initiate point-in-time restore to 5 minutes before corruption
  3. Validate data integrity in restored cluster
  4. Update application connection strings to restored cluster
  5. Resume normal operations

**Scenario 2: Data Corruption (Older than 24 hours)**
- **Trigger**: Data corruption discovered after 24-hour PITR window
- **Recovery Method**: Snapshot restore from daily/weekly/monthly backup
- **RTO**: < 4 hours
- **RPO**: < 24 hours (daily snapshot)
- **Process**:
  1. Identify last known good snapshot before corruption
  2. Restore snapshot to new MongoDB cluster
  3. Validate data integrity
  4. Apply transaction logs if available to minimize data loss
  5. Update application connection strings
  6. Resume normal operations

**Scenario 3: Accidental Collection Drop**
- **Trigger**: Critical collection accidentally deleted
- **Recovery Method**: Point-in-time restore or snapshot restore
- **RTO**: < 1 hour
- **RPO**: < 1 minute (if within PITR window)
- **Process**:
  1. Stop application writes to prevent further changes
  2. Restore collection from PITR or snapshot to temporary cluster
  3. Export affected collection data
  4. Import data to production cluster
  5. Validate data integrity and application functionality
  6. Resume normal operations

**S3 Object Storage Backup**:

**Versioning**:
- **Configuration**: Enabled for all critical buckets (user files, backups, compliance logs)
- **Retention**: 90-day retention for non-current versions
- **MFA Delete**: Enabled for production buckets preventing accidental deletion even by administrators

**Cross-Region Replication**:
- **Source**: us-east-1 primary buckets
- **Destination**: us-west-2 DR buckets
- **Replication Scope**: All objects (including delete markers for disaster recovery)
- **Replication SLA**: Typically < 15 minutes for 99% of objects
- **Use Case**: Regional disaster recovery, regulatory compliance

**Lifecycle Policies**:

| Age | Storage Class | Purpose | Cost Impact |
|-----|--------------|---------|-------------|
| 0-30 days | S3 Standard | Frequent access | Baseline cost |
| 30-90 days | S3 Infrequent Access | Occasional access | 50% cheaper storage |
| 90 days - 7 years | S3 Glacier Deep Archive | Compliance retention | 95% cheaper storage |
| > 7 years | Deleted | Compliance period complete | No cost |

**S3 Restoration Procedures**:

**Scenario 1: Accidental File Deletion**
- **Trigger**: User or application accidentally deletes files
- **Recovery Method**: S3 versioning restore
- **RTO**: < 15 minutes
- **RPO**: 0 (no data loss)
- **Process**:
  1. Identify deleted object and version ID
  2. Restore previous version using S3 console or CLI
  3. Verify file integrity and accessibility
  4. Notify user of restoration

**Scenario 2: Bucket Corruption or Ransomware**
- **Trigger**: Bucket compromised, objects encrypted by malware
- **Recovery Method**: Cross-region replication restore
- **RTO**: < 2 hours
- **RPO**: < 15 minutes
- **Process**:
  1. Isolate compromised bucket (deny all access)
  2. Sync objects from DR region bucket to new production bucket
  3. Update application configuration to new bucket
  4. Validate file accessibility and integrity
  5. Investigate and remediate security breach

**Disaster Recovery Objectives**:

| Disaster Scenario | RTO (Recovery Time) | RPO (Max Data Loss) | Recovery Method |
|-------------------|-------------------|-------------------|-----------------|
| Single Container Failure | < 1 minute | 0 (no data loss) | ECS automatic restart, ALB health check |
| Database Node Failure | < 5 minutes | 0 (replica set) | MongoDB automatic failover to secondary |
| Availability Zone Failure | < 15 minutes | < 5 minutes | Multi-AZ deployment, automatic failover |
| Complete Region Failure | < 4 hours | < 1 hour | DR region activation, cross-region backups |
| Data Corruption | < 2 hours | < 24 hours | Point-in-time restore or snapshot restore |
| Ransomware Attack | < 4 hours | < 15 minutes | Cross-region replication restore |

**Disaster Recovery Testing**:

The infrastructure implements regular disaster recovery drills validating recovery procedures:

- **Quarterly DR Tests**: Full regional failover simulation every quarter
- **Monthly Backup Restores**: Restore production backup to staging environment monthly
- **Continuous Validation**: Automated backup integrity checks daily
- **Documentation**: DR runbooks maintained with step-by-step recovery procedures
- **Team Training**: On-call engineers trained on DR procedures during onboarding

## 8.3 CLOUD SERVICES

### 8.3.1 Cloud Provider Selection and Justification

**Primary Cloud Provider**: **Amazon Web Services (AWS)**

The system leverages AWS as the exclusive cloud provider for all infrastructure and managed services. This cloud-native approach enables the engineering team to focus on application development rather than infrastructure management, reducing time-to-market and operational complexity.

**AWS Selection Rationale**:

**Service Breadth and Maturity**:
- **200+ Services**: Comprehensive catalog covering compute (ECS, EKS, Lambda, EC2), storage (S3, EFS, EBS), databases (RDS, DynamoDB, ElastiCache), networking (VPC, CloudFront, Route 53), security (IAM, KMS, Secrets Manager), monitoring (CloudWatch), and AI/ML (SageMaker, Comprehend)
- **Longest Track Record**: Launched 2006, industry-leading cloud provider with 18+ years operational history
- **Proven Reliability**: Large-scale production deployments by companies including Netflix, Airbnb, Slack demonstrate platform maturity

**Global Infrastructure**:
- **33 Geographic Regions**: Enables future international expansion
- **105 Availability Zones**: Multi-AZ deployment within regions provides high availability
- **450+ CloudFront Edge Locations**: Global content delivery with low-latency access
- **Strategic Regions**: Presence in North America, Europe, Asia Pacific, South America, Middle East, Africa

**Managed Services Philosophy**:
AWS's comprehensive managed services reduce operational overhead:
- **Compute**: ECS/EKS manage container orchestration without manual cluster management
- **Caching**: ElastiCache manages Redis clusters with automatic failover and patching
- **CDN**: CloudFront distributes content globally with automatic scaling
- **Security**: Secrets Manager, KMS, IAM provide turnkey security infrastructure
- **Monitoring**: CloudWatch provides integrated logging, metrics, and alerting

**Security and Compliance**:
- **Certifications**: SOC 1/2/3, ISO 27001, PCI DSS Level 1, HIPAA eligible, GDPR compliant
- **Shared Responsibility Model**: AWS secures infrastructure, application team secures application layer
- **Compliance Inheritance**: Infrastructure automatically inherits AWS compliance certifications
- **Audit Trails**: CloudTrail provides comprehensive API audit logging

**Cost Optimization Tools**:
- **Reserved Instances**: 40-60% cost savings for baseline workloads
- **Savings Plans**: Flexible commitment-based pricing across compute services
- **Spot Instances**: 70-90% cost savings for non-critical workloads (development, batch processing)
- **Cost Explorer**: Granular cost analysis and optimization recommendations
- **Budgets and Alerts**: Proactive cost monitoring preventing overrun

**Ecosystem and Support**:
- **Extensive Documentation**: Comprehensive technical documentation, tutorials, reference architectures
- **Community Resources**: Large community providing troubleshooting assistance, best practices
- **Third-Party Integration**: MongoDB Atlas, Auth0, and other services provide native AWS integration
- **Professional Support**: AWS Enterprise Support option for production workloads if needed

### 8.3.3 High Availability Design

**Multi-Availability Zone Architecture**:

The infrastructure implements comprehensive multi-AZ deployment ensuring no single infrastructure failure causes service disruption:

```
AWS Region: us-east-1
├── Availability Zone A (us-east-1a)
│   ├── Public Subnet (10.0.1.0/24)
│   │   ├── Application Load Balancer Node 1
│   │   └── NAT Gateway A
│   ├── Private Subnet - Application (10.0.11.0/24)
│   │   ├── ECS Task 1 (API Container)
│   │   └── ECS Task 2 (API Container)
│   └── Private Subnet - Data (10.0.21.0/24)
│       └── Redis ElastiCache Node 1
│
├── Availability Zone B (us-east-1b)
│   ├── Public Subnet (10.0.2.0/24)
│   │   ├── Application Load Balancer Node 2
│   │   └── NAT Gateway B
│   ├── Private Subnet - Application (10.0.12.0/24)
│   │   ├── ECS Task 3 (API Container)
│   │   └── ECS Task 4 (API Container)
│   └── Private Subnet - Data (10.0.22.0/24)
│       └── Redis ElastiCache Node 2
│
└── Availability Zone C (us-east-1c)
    └── Private Subnet - Application (10.0.13.0/24)
        ├── ECS Task 5 (API Container)
        └── ECS Task 6 (API Container)

MongoDB Atlas Replica Set (Managed Multi-AZ):
├── Node 1 (Primary) - AZ B
├── Node 2 (Secondary) - AZ A
└── Node 3 (Secondary) - AZ C
```

**High Availability Mechanisms by Layer**:

**Application Layer (ECS Tasks)**:
- **Distribution**: Containers distributed evenly across 2-3 availability zones
- **Minimum Healthy**: 50% minimum during deployments ensures availability
- **Maximum Running**: 200% maximum allows doubling capacity during rolling updates
- **Health Checks**: ALB health checks every 30 seconds with 3-failure threshold
- **Automatic Replacement**: Unhealthy containers automatically terminated and replaced
- **Failure Impact**: Single AZ failure impacts maximum 33-50% of capacity, with automatic recovery

**Load Balancer Layer (ALB)**:
- **Multi-AZ Deployment**: ALB nodes automatically deployed across all availability zones
- **Health-Based Routing**: Traffic only routed to healthy containers passing health checks
- **Connection Draining**: 30-second draining period during container replacement
- **Automatic Scaling**: ALB capacity scales automatically based on traffic volume
- **Failure Impact**: ALB multi-AZ architecture provides automatic node failover

**Database Layer (MongoDB Atlas)**:
- **Replica Set**: 3-node replica set (1 primary + 2 secondaries) across 3 availability zones
- **Automatic Failover**: Primary election within 10-30 seconds on primary failure
- **Write Availability**: Maintained through automatic primary promotion from secondaries
- **Read Availability**: Read-only operations continue on secondaries during failover
- **Failure Impact**: Single node failure triggers automatic failover with < 30s disruption

**Cache Layer (Redis ElastiCache)**:
- **Cluster Mode**: Redis cluster with multiple shards for horizontal scaling
- **Multi-AZ Replication**: Each shard has primary and replica nodes across AZs
- **Automatic Failover**: Replica promotion to primary within 60 seconds
- **Failure Mode**: Cache unavailable during failover, application falls back to MongoDB queries

**Storage Layer (S3)**:
- **Multi-AZ Storage**: S3 automatically replicates objects across AZs within region
- **Durability**: 99.999999999% (11 nines) annual durability
- **Availability**: 99.99% annual availability SLA
- **Failure Impact**: S3 architecture transparent to availability zone failures

**Availability Targets and Guarantees**:

| Component | Availability SLA | Downtime/Month | Failover Time | Failure Impact |
|-----------|-----------------|----------------|---------------|----------------|
| **Overall System** | 99.5% | ~3.6 hours | 15 minutes | Multi-AZ architecture |
| **Application Layer** | 99.9% | ~43 minutes | < 3 minutes | Container restart + health check |
| **Load Balancer** | 99.99% | ~4 minutes | Automatic | Multi-AZ, no failover needed |
| **MongoDB Atlas** | 99.95% | ~22 minutes | 10-30 seconds | Automatic replica election |
| **Redis ElastiCache** | Best effort | Variable | < 60 seconds | Graceful fallback to database |
| **S3 Storage** | 99.99% | ~4 minutes | Transparent | Multi-AZ, automatic |

**Single Point of Failure Analysis**:

The architecture eliminates single points of failure through redundancy:

✅ **Application Containers**: Multiple containers across multiple AZs
✅ **Load Balancer**: Multi-AZ ALB with automatic node management
✅ **Database**: 3-node replica set with automatic failover
✅ **Cache**: Multi-AZ cluster with replica promotion
✅ **Storage**: S3 multi-AZ replication by default
✅ **Network**: NAT Gateways in each AZ for outbound connectivity
❌ **Auth0**: External SaaS dependency (mitigation: JWKS caching enables continued JWT validation during Auth0 outages)
❌ **LLM Providers**: External SaaS dependencies (mitigation: multi-provider fallback chain OpenAI → Anthropic → cached responses)

### 8.3.4 Cost Optimization Strategy

**Resource Right-Sizing**:

Initial resource allocation based on anticipated load with continuous monitoring enabling optimization:

**Container Sizing Evolution**:

| Phase | Container Spec | Rationale | Monthly Cost (4 containers) |
|-------|---------------|-----------|----------------------------|
| **Initial (Conservative)** | 2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM | Safety buffer for unknown load patterns | ~$150-200 |
| **After 30 Days** | Resize based on utilization | Data-driven optimization | Variable |
| **Optimized Target** | 60-80% avg utilization | Balance performance and cost | ~$120-180 |

**Monitoring and Optimization Process**:
1. **Baseline Period**: Deploy with conservative sizing for 30 days
2. **Data Collection**: CloudWatch metrics track actual CPU/memory utilization
3. **Analysis**: Identify sustained utilization patterns (P50, P95, P99 percentiles)
4. **Adjustment**: Resize containers if sustained utilization < 40% or > 80%
5. **Validation**: Monitor for 7 days post-adjustment, repeat if needed

**Auto-Scaling Cost Management**:

**Baseline vs. Peak Capacity Strategy**:

```
Cost Model:
├── Baseline (4 containers, always running): Reserved capacity pricing
│   └── Savings: 40-60% vs on-demand
├── Peak Traffic (scale to 20 containers): On-demand pricing
│   └── Cost: Higher per-hour, but only during peak periods
└── Total Monthly Cost: Baseline reserved + average peak on-demand
```

**Auto-Scaling Configuration for Cost Control**:

| Parameter | Value | Cost Impact |
|-----------|-------|-------------|
| **Minimum Containers** | 2 (HA requirement) | Baseline cost floor |
| **Typical Containers** | 4-6 (normal traffic) | Reserved capacity target |
| **Maximum Containers** | 20 (configurable limit) | Cost ceiling prevents runaway scaling |
| **Scale-In Cooldown** | 5 minutes | Prevents thrashing, reduces churn costs |
| **Scale-Out Aggressiveness** | Medium | Balance responsiveness vs cost |

**Reserved Capacity Strategy**:

**Reserved Instance / Savings Plan Approach**:

| Capacity Type | Usage Pattern | Discount | Application |
|--------------|---------------|----------|-------------|
| **Reserved (1-year)** | Baseline 4 containers, always running | 40% vs on-demand | Production baseline capacity |
| **Reserved (3-year)** | After product-market fit validation | 60% vs on-demand | Long-term baseline after 1-year operation |
| **On-Demand** | Peak traffic, scale from 4 → 20 containers | No discount | Flexibility for growth |
| **Spot Instances** | Development/staging environments | 70% vs on-demand | Non-production workloads |

**Estimated Cost Savings**:

```
Scenario: 4 containers baseline, average 8 containers
├── All On-Demand: $400/month
├── Reserved Baseline (4) + On-Demand Peak (4 avg): $240 + $100 = $340/month
└── Savings: $60/month (15% reduction)

After 1 Year (higher confidence):
├── Reserved Baseline (6) + On-Demand Peak (2 avg): $216 + $50 = $266/month
└── Savings: $134/month (33% reduction)
```

**Data Lifecycle Management**:

**S3 Storage Cost Optimization**:

| Age | Storage Class | Cost per GB/Month | Retrieval Cost | Use Case |
|-----|--------------|-------------------|----------------|----------|
| **0-30 days** | S3 Standard | $0.023 | None | Frequent access |
| **30-90 days** | S3 Infrequent Access | $0.0125 (46% cheaper) | $0.01/GB | Occasional access |
| **90 days - 7 years** | S3 Glacier Deep Archive | $0.00099 (96% cheaper) | $0.02/GB + 12h retrieval | Compliance retention |
| **> 7 years** | Deleted | $0 | N/A | Compliance period complete |

**Estimated Storage Cost Progression**:

```
Example: 1 TB active data
├── Month 0-1: 1 TB @ S3 Standard = $23/month
├── Month 2: 0.9 TB Standard + 0.1 TB IA = $20.70 + $1.25 = $21.95/month
├── Month 4: 0.7 TB Standard + 0.2 TB IA + 0.1 TB Glacier = $16.10 + $2.50 + $0.10 = $18.70/month
└── Savings: 19% after 4 months lifecycle transitions
```

**Lifecycle Policy Configuration**:

```json
{
  "Rules": [
    {
      "Id": "TransitionToIA",
      "Status": "Enabled",
      "Transitions": [
        {
          "Days": 30,
          "StorageClass": "STANDARD_IA"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "Id": "TransitionToGlacier",
      "Status": "Enabled",

        {
          "Days": 90,
          "StorageClass": "DEEP_ARCHIVE"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "Id": "DeleteAfterRetention",
      "Status": "Enabled",
      "Expiration": {
        "Days": 2555
      }
    }
  ]

```

**Cache Optimization for Cost Reduction**:

**Redis Cache Strategy**:

Aggressive caching reduces database query volume and enables lower-tier database cluster selection:

| Cache Hit Rate | Database Load Reduction | Potential Database Tier Savings |
|----------------|------------------------|--------------------------------|
| **40%** | 40% fewer queries | Minimal tier reduction |
| **70% (target)** | 70% fewer queries | M30 → M20 potential ($200/month savings) |
| **85% (optimized)** | 85% fewer queries | M30 → M10 potential ($400/month savings) |

**Cache Configuration for Cost Optimization**:

| Data Type | TTL | Rationale | Cost Impact |
|-----------|-----|-----------|-------------|
| **User Profiles** | 15 minutes | Reduce database load for frequent profile lookups | High impact |
| **LLM Responses** | 1 hour | Expensive LLM API cost reduction ($0.01-0.06 per request) | Very high impact |
| **API Responses** | 5 minutes | Reduce compute and database load | Medium impact |
| **Session Data** | 30 minutes | Reduce authentication overhead | Medium impact |

**LLM API Cost Optimization**:

LLM API costs represent significant operational expense requiring active management:

**Cost Factors**:
- **OpenAI GPT-4**: $0.03 per 1K input tokens, $0.06 per 1K output tokens
- **Anthropic Claude**: Similar pricing structure
- **Average Request**: 1,000 input tokens, 500 output tokens = $0.06 per request
- **Target Volume**: 10,000 requests/day = $600/day = $18,000/month

**Cost Optimization Strategies**:

| Strategy | Implementation | Estimated Savings |
|----------|----------------|-------------------|
| **Response Caching** | 1-hour TTL in Redis for similar queries | 40-60% (cache hit rate dependent) |
| **Prompt Optimization** | Reduce system prompt verbosity, context window optimization | 10-20% |
| **Model Selection** | Route simple queries to cheaper models (GPT-3.5) | 20-30% |
| **Rate Limiting** | Enforce per-user quotas preventing abuse | Variable (prevents runaway costs) |
| **Semantic Deduplication** | Vector similarity search before LLM call | 10-20% |

**Combined LLM Cost Optimization Impact**:

```
Baseline: $18,000/month (no optimization)
├── Caching (50% hit rate): $9,000/month saved
├── Prompt Optimization (15%): $1,350/month saved
├── Model Selection (25% to cheaper model, 80% cost reduction): $900/month saved
└── Optimized Total: ~$6,750/month (63% reduction)
```

**Spot Instance Strategy**:

**Development and Staging Environments**:

| Environment | Spot Instance Usage | Discount | Interruption Handling |
|-------------|-------------------|----------|----------------------|
| **Development** | 100% spot instances | 70% cost reduction | Automatic replacement, acceptable brief downtime |
| **Staging** | 50-75% spot instances | 35-52% average discount | Graceful degradation, on-demand fallback |
| **Production** | 0% spot instances | Not applicable | Reliability priority |

**Spot Instance Savings Calculation**:

```
Development Environment:
├── On-Demand Cost: 4 containers × $0.05/hour × 730 hours = $146/month
├── Spot Instance Cost: 4 containers × $0.015/hour × 730 hours = $44/month
└── Savings: $102/month (70% reduction)

Staging Environment:
├── On-Demand Cost: 4 containers × $0.10/hour × 730 hours = $292/month
├── Mixed (50% spot): (2 × $0.03 + 2 × $0.10) × 730 = $190/month
└── Savings: $102/month (35% reduction)
```

**Estimated Monthly Infrastructure Costs**:

| Environment | Compute | Database | Cache | Storage | Network | Total |
|-------------|---------|----------|-------|---------|---------|-------|
| **Development** | $50 (spot) | $50 (M10) | $15 (t3.micro) | $25 | $10 | **~$150/month** |
| **Staging** | $150 (mixed) | $100 (M20) | $30 (m5.large) | $50 | $20 | **~$350/month** |
| **Production (Initial)** | $250-400 (4-6 reserved + on-demand) | $300 (M30) | $150 (r6g.large) | $100 | $50 | **~$850-1,000/month** |
| **Production (Scaled)** | $600-1,000 (20 containers peak) | $600 (M40/M50) | $300 (cluster) | $200 | $100 | **~$1,800-2,200/month** |

### 8.3.5 Security and Compliance Considerations

**Encryption**:

**Data at Rest**:

| Service | Encryption Method | Key Management | Rotation Policy |
|---------|------------------|----------------|-----------------|
| **MongoDB Atlas** | AES-256 via WiredTiger storage engine | AWS KMS (Customer-Managed Key) | 90-day automatic rotation |
| **Amazon S3** | SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS | AWS-managed (SSE-S3) or Customer-managed (SSE-KMS) | Automatic (SSE-S3) or 90-day (SSE-KMS) |
| **Redis ElastiCache** | Optional encryption at rest for AOF persistence | AWS KMS | 90-day automatic rotation |
| **AWS Secrets Manager** | AES-256 encryption | AWS KMS | 90-day automatic rotation |
| **EBS Volumes** (if used) | AES-256 encryption | AWS-managed or customer-managed KMS key | 90-day rotation |

**Data in Transit**:

| Connection | Encryption Protocol | Certificate Management | Configuration |
|------------|-------------------|----------------------|---------------|
| **Client → ALB** | TLS 1.3 / TLS 1.2 | AWS Certificate Manager | Auto-renewal, wildcard cert |
| **ALB → Containers** | HTTP within VPC | N/A (trusted network) | Security groups restrict access |
| **Application → MongoDB** | TLS 1.2+ | MongoDB Atlas managed | Certificate validation enabled |
| **Application → Redis** | TLS (optional) | AWS managed | Within VPC, optional encryption |
| **Application → External APIs** | HTTPS | Public CA certificates | Certificate validation enforced |

**Cipher Suite Configuration**:

ALB SSL policy enforces strong cipher suites with forward secrecy:

**Preferred Cipher Suites** (TLS 1.3):
- TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
- TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256
- TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256

**Supported Cipher Suites** (TLS 1.2):
- TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
- TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
- TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256

**Disabled (Insecure)**:
- All TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 cipher suites
- All cipher suites without forward secrecy (non-ECDHE)
- RC4, 3DES, MD5-based cipher suites

**Network Security**:

**VPC Architecture**:

```
VPC: 6nove4-production (10.0.0.0/16)
├── Public Subnets (Internet-Accessible)
│   ├── 10.0.1.0/24 (AZ-A) - ALB, NAT Gateway
│   ├── 10.0.2.0/24 (AZ-B) - ALB, NAT Gateway
│   └── 10.0.3.0/24 (AZ-C) - NAT Gateway
├── Private Subnets - Application Tier (No Direct Internet)
│   ├── 10.0.11.0/24 (AZ-A) - ECS Tasks
│   ├── 10.0.12.0/24 (AZ-B) - ECS Tasks
│   └── 10.0.13.0/24 (AZ-C) - ECS Tasks
└── Private Subnets - Data Tier (No Direct Internet)
    ├── 10.0.21.0/24 (AZ-A) - Redis ElastiCache
    └── 10.0.22.0/24 (AZ-B) - Redis ElastiCache
```

**Security Group Rules**:

**ALB Security Group**:
- **Inbound**: HTTPS (443) from 0.0.0.0/0 (internet)
- **Outbound**: HTTP (80) to application container security group only

**Application Container Security Group**:
- **Inbound**: HTTP (80) from ALB security group only
- **Outbound**: 
  - MongoDB (27017) to MongoDB Atlas IPs (IP whitelisting)
  - Redis (6379) to cache security group
  - HTTPS (443) to 0.0.0.0/0 (external APIs: Auth0, OpenAI, AWS services)

**Redis Cache Security Group**:
- **Inbound**: Redis (6379) from application container security group only
- **Outbound**: None required

**MongoDB Atlas** (External, IP Whitelist):
- **Allowed IPs**: NAT Gateway elastic IPs from all AZs (static IPs)
- **Denied**: All other IPs (default deny)

**Network ACLs**:

Network ACLs provide additional layer of defense (stateless firewall):
- **Public Subnets**: Allow inbound 443, ephemeral outbound ports
- **Private Subnets**: Allow inbound from VPC CIDR only, outbound as needed

**Access Control**:

**IAM Role-Based Authentication**:

The architecture implements least-privilege IAM roles for service-to-service authentication:

| IAM Role | Purpose | Permissions | Attached To |
|----------|---------|-------------|-------------|
| **ECSTaskExecutionRole** | ECS task launch | ECR pull, CloudWatch logs, Secrets Manager read | ECS service |
| **ECSTaskRole** | Application runtime | S3 read/write, Secrets Manager read, CloudWatch metrics/logs | ECS task |
| **LambdaExecutionRole** | Lambda function runtime | CloudWatch logs, Secrets Manager read, specific resource access | Lambda functions |
| **MongoDBAtlasEncryptionRole** | MongoDB encryption | KMS decrypt/encrypt for MongoDB Atlas | MongoDB Atlas service |

**Example ECS Task Role Policy** (Least Privilege):

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "s3:GetObject",
        "s3:PutObject",
        "s3:DeleteObject"
      ],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::6nove4-user-files-prod/*"
    },
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "secretsmanager:GetSecretValue"
      ],
      "Resource": [
        "arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-east-1:ACCOUNT:secret:prod/mongodb-uri*",
        "arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-east-1:ACCOUNT:secret:prod/redis-url*"
      ]
    },
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "logs:CreateLogStream",
        "logs:PutLogEvents"
      ],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:logs:us-east-1:ACCOUNT:log-group:/ecs/6nove4/production/*"
    }
  ]
}
```

**Key Principles**:
- **No Long-Lived Credentials**: IAM roles provide temporary credentials, no API keys stored in code
- **Least Privilege**: Roles grant minimum permissions required for function
- **Explicit Deny**: Default deny with explicit allows
- **Resource-Specific**: Permissions scoped to specific resources (buckets, secrets, log groups)

**MFA Requirements**:
- **Console Access**: MFA required for all AWS console access (IAM users)
- **Administrative Actions**: Sensitive operations require MFA re-authentication
- **API Access**: Applications use IAM roles, no console access needed

**Compliance Monitoring** (From Section 8.2.1.4):

**GDPR Compliance**:
- **Right to Erasure**: 30-day deadline tracking with automated alerts
- **Right to Access**: Data export within 45 days
- **Audit Trail**: All deletion events logged and retained 7 years

**SOC 2 Compliance**:
- **Security Controls**: RBAC, encryption, monitoring continuously validated
- **Availability**: 99.5% uptime target tracked with monthly reporting
- **Processing Integrity**: Input validation, error handling, transaction controls

**CCPA Compliance**:
- **Data Deletion**: Shared with GDPR procedures
- **Data Export**: User-initiated data export functionality
- **Opt-Out**: Not applicable (no data sale)

**Audit Logging**:

**CloudTrail Configuration**:
- **All Regions**: Multi-region trail captures API calls across all regions
- **All Services**: Covers IAM, KMS, S3, ECS, Secrets Manager, all AWS services
- **Log File Validation**: Cryptographic signing prevents tampering
- **S3 Storage**: Immutable logs with object lock enabled
- **Retention**: 7 years in S3 Glacier for compliance

**CloudWatch Logs**:
- **Application Logs**: Structured JSON logs from all containers
- **Security Events**: Authentication, authorization, access attempts
- **Retention**: 30 days (production), 7 days (dev/staging)
- **Archive**: S3 export for 7-year compliance retention

## 8.4 CONTAINERIZATION

### 8.4.1 Container Platform Selection

**Platform**: **Docker**

Docker serves as the container platform for application packaging, providing consistent execution environments across development, staging, and production deployments.

**Docker Selection Rationale**:

| Factor | Docker Advantage | Business Impact |
|--------|-----------------|-----------------|
| **Industry Standard** | De facto container standard, widespread adoption | Minimal learning curve, extensive community resources |
| **AWS Integration** | Native support in ECS, EKS, ECR | Seamless deployment to AWS infrastructure |
| **Portability** | Consistent execution across local development, CI/CD, cloud | Reduces "works on my machine" issues |
| **Resource Efficiency** | Lightweight compared to VMs (seconds startup vs minutes) | Cost-effective, fast scaling |
| **Ecosystem** | Docker Hub, registries, tooling, documentation | Accelerated development, pre-built base images |
| **Build Optimization** | Multi-stage builds, layer caching, BuildKit | Fast builds, small images |

**Docker Version**: Latest stable release (Docker Engine 24.x+)

**Container Registry**: Amazon ECR (Elastic Container Registry)
- **Vulnerability Scanning**: Automatic scanning on image push
- **Image Signing**: Support for Docker Content Trust
- **Lifecycle Policies**: Automatic cleanup of old images (retain last 30 images)
- **Cross-Region Replication**: DR region replication for disaster recovery

### 8.4.2 Base Image Strategy

**Backend Service (Python/Flask)**:

**Base Image**: `python:3.11-slim`

**Selection Rationale**:
- **Slim Variant**: Reduces image size by 60-70% compared to full Python image (150 MB vs 450+ MB)
- **Official Image**: Maintained by Docker Python team, security updates, best practices
- **Python 3.11**: Latest stable Python with performance improvements (10-60% faster than Python 3.10)
- **Debian-Based**: Slim images based on Debian Bullseye, familiar package manager (apt)

**Alternative Base Images Considered**:

| Base Image | Size | Pros | Cons | Decision |
|------------|------|------|------|----------|
| **python:3.11** (full) | 920 MB | All packages included, no build issues | Unnecessarily large, increased attack surface | ❌ Rejected |
| **python:3.11-slim** | 150 MB | Smaller size, essential packages only | May need additional system dependencies | ✅ Selected |
| **python:3.11-alpine** | 50 MB | Smallest size, minimal attack surface | musl libc incompatibility issues, longer build times | ❌ Rejected (compatibility) |

**Multi-Stage Build Strategy**:

Docker multi-stage builds separate build dependencies from runtime dependencies, significantly reducing final image size:

**Dockerfile Structure** (Illustrative Example from Technical Specification):

```dockerfile
# Stage 1: Build Stage
FROM python:3.11-slim AS builder

#### Install build dependencies
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    gcc \
    libpq-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

#### Set working directory
WORKDIR /app

#### Copy dependency files
COPY requirements.txt .

#### Install Python dependencies
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir --user -r requirements.txt

#### Stage 2: Runtime Stage
FROM python:3.11-slim

#### Install only runtime system dependencies
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    libpq5 \
    curl \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

#### Set working directory
WORKDIR /app

#### Copy Python dependencies from builder stage
COPY --from=builder /root/.local /root/.local

#### Copy application code
COPY . .

#### Create non-root user for security
RUN useradd -m -u 1000 appuser && \
    chown -R appuser:appuser /app

#### Switch to non-root user
USER appuser

#### Make Python dependencies available
ENV PATH=/root/.local/bin:$PATH

#### Expose application port
EXPOSE 5000

#### Health check endpoint
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --start-period=60s --retries=3 \
  CMD curl -f http://localhost:5000/health || exit 1

#### Start application with Gunicorn
CMD ["gunicorn", "--bind", "0.0.0.0:5000", "--workers", "4", "--threads", "2", "--timeout", "30", "app:app"]
```

**Multi-Stage Build Benefits**:

| Metric | Single-Stage Build | Multi-Stage Build | Improvement |
|--------|-------------------|-------------------|-------------|
| **Image Size** | 600-800 MB | 200-300 MB | 50-70% reduction |
| **Build Dependencies** | Included in final image | Excluded from final image | Smaller attack surface |
| **Build Time** (cached) | 30-60 seconds | 10-20 seconds | Layer caching optimization |
| **Security** | More packages = more vulnerabilities | Minimal packages = fewer vulnerabilities | Reduced CVE exposure |

**Frontend Applications**:

**Web Application (React/TypeScript)**:

**Build Stage**: Node.js 20 for building React application
```dockerfile
FROM node:20-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production
COPY . .
RUN npm run build
```

**Runtime Stage**: Nginx for serving static files
```dockerfile
FROM nginx:alpine
COPY --from=build /app/dist /usr/share/nginx/html
COPY nginx.conf /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
EXPOSE 80
CMD ["nginx", "-g", "daemon off;"]
```

**Result**: 
- **Build Image**: 1.2 GB (not deployed)
- **Runtime Image**: 25 MB (nginx + static files)
- **Optimization**: 98% size reduction for deployed image

**Mobile and Desktop Applications**:

- **Mobile (React Native)**: Built natively for iOS and Android, not containerized
- **Desktop (Electron)**: Packaged as native installers (DMG, EXE, AppImage), not containerized

### 8.4.3 Image Versioning Approach

**Semantic Versioning**: Container images follow semantic versioning `{service}:{major}.{minor}.{patch}`

**Tagging Strategy**:

| Tag Format | Example | Purpose | Mutability |
|------------|---------|---------|------------|
| **Semantic Version** | `api-server:1.2.3` | Specific release version | Immutable |
| **Minor Version** | `api-server:1.2` | Latest patch in minor version | Mutable (updated) |
| **Major Version** | `api-server:1` | Latest minor in major version | Mutable (updated) |
| **Latest** | `api-server:latest` | Latest stable production release | Mutable (updated) |
| **Git SHA** | `api-server:abc123f` | Commit-specific build | Immutable |
| **Environment** | `api-server:dev`, `api-server:staging` | Environment-specific builds | Mutable (updated) |

**Tagging Workflow Example**:

```bash
# Build image with multiple tags
docker build -t 123456789.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/api-server:1.2.3 \
             -t 123456789.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/api-server:1.2 \
             -t 123456789.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/api-server:1 \
             -t 123456789.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/api-server:latest \
             -t 123456789.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/api-server:$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) \
             .

#### Push all tags to ECR
docker push 123456789.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/api-server --all-tags
```

**Versioning Best Practices**:

**Immutable Tags**:
- Specific versions (`1.2.3`) and Git SHAs (`abc123f`) never change
- Enables guaranteed reproducibility and rollback
- Production deployments reference specific versions: `api-server:1.2.3`

**Mutable Tags**:
- `latest`, `dev`, `staging` updated with each build
- Development environments use mutable tags for convenience
- Production environments NEVER use mutable tags

**Git Integration**:
- Every build tagged with Git commit SHA for traceability
- Enables correlation between deployed image and source code version
- Simplifies debugging and rollback: "What code is running in production?" → Check image tag → Find Git commit

**ECR Lifecycle Policy**:

Automatic cleanup prevents registry bloat and reduces storage costs:

```json
{
  "rules": [
    {
      "rulePriority": 1,
      "description": "Keep last 30 images by semantic version",
      "selection": {
        "tagStatus": "tagged",
        "tagPrefixList": ["1."],
        "countType": "imageCountMoreThan",
        "countNumber": 30
      },
      "action": {
        "type": "expire"
      }
    },
    {
      "rulePriority": 2,
      "description": "Delete untagged images after 7 days",
      "selection": {
        "tagStatus": "untagged",
        "countType": "sinceImagePushed",
        "countUnit": "days",
        "countNumber": 7
      },
      "action": {
        "type": "expire"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

### 8.4.4 Build Optimization Techniques

**Layer Caching Optimization**:

Docker builds images in layers, caching unchanged layers for faster subsequent builds. Optimize Dockerfile instruction order from least to most frequently changed:

**Optimal Layer Order**:

1. **Base Image** (`FROM python:3.11-slim`) - Changes rarely (Python version upgrades)
2. **System Dependencies** (`RUN apt-get install`) - Changes rarely
3. **Python Dependencies** (`COPY requirements.txt`, `RUN pip install`) - Changes occasionally
4. **Application Code** (`COPY . .`) - Changes frequently

**Impact of Incorrect Layer Order**:

```dockerfile
# ❌ Bad: Application code copied before dependencies
FROM python:3.11-slim
COPY . .                    # Changes frequently
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt  # Invalidates cache every time

#### ✅ Good: Dependencies cached separately
FROM python:3.11-slim
COPY requirements.txt .     # Changes occasionally
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt  # Cached unless requirements.txt changes
COPY . .                    # Changes frequently, but doesn't invalidate dependency cache
```

**Build Time Comparison**:

| Scenario | Bad Layer Order | Good Layer Order | Time Savings |
|----------|----------------|------------------|--------------|
| **First Build** | 180 seconds | 180 seconds | 0% (both full build) |
| **Code Change** | 180 seconds (full rebuild) | 15 seconds (cached layers) | 92% faster |
| **Dependency Change** | 180 seconds | 165 seconds | 8% faster |

**BuildKit Optimization**:

Docker BuildKit provides advanced build features:

```bash
# Enable BuildKit for faster builds
export DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1

#### BuildKit features:
#### - Parallel layer building
#### - Improved layer caching
#### - Build secrets (avoid secrets in image history)
#### - SSH forwarding (for private repositories)
```

**Build Secrets** (Avoid secrets in image layers):

```dockerfile
# ❌ Bad: Secrets visible in image history
RUN echo "API_KEY=secret123" >> /etc/config

#### ✅ Good: BuildKit secrets (not persisted in layers)
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=api_key \
    API_KEY=$(cat /run/secrets/api_key) && \
    configure_application "$API_KEY"
```

**Minimal Base Images**:

Smaller base images provide multiple benefits:

| Base Image | Size | Security Vulnerabilities (Typical) | Build Time |
|------------|------|-----------------------------------|------------|
| **python:3.11** (full) | 920 MB | 200+ packages, higher CVE count | Fast (all tools available) |
| **python:3.11-slim** | 150 MB | Essential packages, moderate CVE count | Medium (may need build deps) |
| **python:3.11-alpine** | 50 MB | Minimal packages, lowest CVE count | Slow (musl libc compilation) |

**Best Practices Summary**:

1. **Order Dockerfile from Least to Most Frequently Changed**
   - Base image → system dependencies → application dependencies → application code
   - Maximizes layer caching effectiveness

2. **Use Multi-Stage Builds**
   - Separate build dependencies from runtime dependencies
   - Reduces final image size by 50-70%

3. **Minimize Layer Count**
   - Combine related RUN commands with `&&`
   - Reduces image size and improves build performance

4. **Clean Up in Same Layer**
   - `apt-get clean` and `rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*` in same RUN command
   - Prevents cleanup from creating separate layers that don't reduce size

5. **Use .dockerignore**
   - Exclude unnecessary files from build context (node_modules, .git, __pycache__)
   - Faster context upload, smaller images

6. **Non-Root User**
   - Run application as non-root user (security best practice)
   - Creates dedicated user with minimal permissions

7. **Health Checks**
   - Include HEALTHCHECK instruction for orchestration platform integration
   - Enables automatic unhealthy container detection and replacement

### 8.4.5 Security Scanning Requirements

**Container Registry**: **Amazon ECR** with integrated vulnerability scanning

**Scanning Configuration**:

**Scan on Push**: 
- Automatically triggered when images pushed to ECR
- Powered by Clair (open-source vulnerability scanner)
- Scans all layers for known CVEs (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures)
- Results available within 5-15 minutes of push

**Continuous Scanning**:
- Images rescanned when CVE databases updated
- New vulnerabilities detected in previously scanned images
- Ensures ongoing security posture monitoring

**Scan Coverage**:
- **Operating System Packages**: Debian/Ubuntu (apt), Alpine (apk), Red Hat (yum)
- **Language-Specific Dependencies**: Python (pip), Node.js (npm), Java (Maven/Gradle), Ruby (gem)
- **CVE Database**: Updated daily from NVD (National Vulnerability Database)

**Severity Classification**:

| Severity | Definition | Response |
|----------|-----------|----------|
| **CRITICAL** | Exploitable vulnerability with severe impact (RCE, privilege escalation) | **Block deployment**, immediate remediation required |
| **HIGH** | Significant vulnerability with workaround or limited exploitability | **Warning**, remediation within 7 days, deploy with approval |
| **MEDIUM** | Moderate vulnerability with known mitigations | **Informational**, remediation within 30 days |
| **LOW** | Minor vulnerability or theoretical exploit | **Informational**, best-effort remediation |
| **INFORMATIONAL** | No vulnerability, configuration recommendation | **Optional**, consider implementing |

**CI/CD Integration** (GitHub Actions):

**Security Scan Pipeline**:

```yaml
name: Build and Scan Docker Image

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  build-and-scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v3
      
      - name: Configure AWS credentials
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v2
        with:
          aws-access-key-id: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
          aws-secret-access-key: ${{ secrets.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
          aws-region: us-east-1
      
      - name: Login to Amazon ECR
        id: login-ecr
        uses: aws-actions/amazon-ecr-login@v1
      
      - name: Build Docker image
        env:
          ECR_REGISTRY: ${{ steps.login-ecr.outputs.registry }}
          ECR_REPOSITORY: api-server
          IMAGE_TAG: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          docker build -t $ECR_REGISTRY/$ECR_REPOSITORY:$IMAGE_TAG .
      
      - name: Run Trivy security scan (local)
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@master
        with:
          image-ref: ${{ steps.login-ecr.outputs.registry }}/api-server:${{ github.sha }}
          format: 'json'
          output: 'trivy-results.json'
          severity: 'CRITICAL,HIGH'
      
      - name: Check for CRITICAL vulnerabilities
        run: |
          CRITICAL_COUNT=$(jq '[.Results[].Vulnerabilities[]? | select(.Severity=="CRITICAL")] | length' trivy-results.json)
          if [ "$CRITICAL_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "❌ Found $CRITICAL_COUNT CRITICAL vulnerabilities - blocking deployment"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "✅ No CRITICAL vulnerabilities found"
      
      - name: Check for HIGH vulnerabilities
        run: |
          HIGH_COUNT=$(jq '[.Results[].Vulnerabilities[]? | select(.Severity=="HIGH")] | length' trivy-results.json)
          if [ "$HIGH_COUNT" -gt 5 ]; then
            echo "⚠️  Found $HIGH_COUNT HIGH vulnerabilities - review required"
            # Don't block, but flag for review
          fi
      
      - name: Push image to ECR
        if: success()
        env:
          ECR_REGISTRY: ${{ steps.login-ecr.outputs.registry }}
          ECR_REPOSITORY: api-server
          IMAGE_TAG: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          docker push $ECR_REGISTRY/$ECR_REPOSITORY:$IMAGE_TAG
      
      - name: ECR Image Scan
        run: |
          aws ecr start-image-scan \
            --repository-name api-server \
            --image-id imageTag=${{ github.sha }}
```

**Vulnerability Response Workflow**:

**CRITICAL Vulnerability Detected**:
1. **Immediate Action**: Block deployment to production
2. **Investigation**: Security team investigates exploitability and impact
3. **Remediation Options**:
   - Update base image to patched version
   - Update vulnerable dependency to patched version
   - Apply temporary mitigation (WAF rule, network restrictions) if no patch available
4. **Validation**: Rebuild image, rescan, verify CRITICAL vulnerability resolved
5. **Deployment**: Resume deployment after resolution
6. **Timeframe**: Same day (P0 priority)

**HIGH Vulnerability Detected**:
1. **Warning**: Allow deployment with explicit approval (engineering manager)
2. **Remediation**: Create ticket for remediation within 7 days
3. **Tracking**: Vulnerability dashboard tracks remediation status
4. **Escalation**: Escalate to security team if not resolved within 7 days

**MEDIUM/LOW Vulnerability Detected**:
1. **Informational**: Log vulnerability, create backlog ticket
2. **Prioritization**: Address during regular maintenance window
3. **Remediation**: Best effort within 30 days (MEDIUM) or next sprint (LOW)

**Dependency Scanning (Supplementary)**:

In addition to container scanning, scan application dependencies directly:

**Python (pip)**:
```bash
# Scan Python dependencies
pip-audit --requirement requirements.txt
```

**Node.js (npm)**:
```bash
# Scan Node.js dependencies
npm audit --production
```

**Third-Party Tools**:
- **Snyk**: SaaS vulnerability scanning with IDE integration
- **Trivy**: Open-source vulnerability scanner (used in CI/CD pipeline above)
- **Grype**: Open-source vulnerability scanner by Anchore
- **Clair**: Open-source vulnerability scanner (powers ECR scanning)

**Continuous Monitoring**:

**Vulnerability Dashboard**:
- Aggregate vulnerability counts by severity across all images
- Track vulnerability age and remediation status
- Alert when new CRITICAL/HIGH vulnerabilities detected in production images

**Automated Alerts**:
- Slack/Email notification on CRITICAL vulnerability detection
- Weekly digest of HIGH vulnerabilities requiring remediation
- Monthly vulnerability trend report

## 8.5 ORCHESTRATION

### 8.5.1 Orchestration Platform Selection

**Platform**: **AWS ECS (Elastic Container Service)** (Initial Recommendation) with evolution to **AWS EKS (Elastic Kubernetes Service)** based on scale requirements

**Initial Platform: AWS ECS**

**ECS Selection Rationale**:

| Factor | ECS Advantage | Business Impact |
|--------|---------------|-----------------|
| **Operational Simplicity** | No control plane management, AWS manages cluster infrastructure | Lower operational overhead for small teams |
| **AWS Native Integration** | Seamless integration with ALB, CloudWatch, IAM, Secrets Manager, ECR | Reduced integration complexity |
| **Cost Efficiency** | No control plane costs (EKS: $0.10/hour = $73/month per cluster) | Lower infrastructure costs for initial scale |
| **Learning Curve** | Simpler mental model than Kubernetes | Faster onboarding for engineers new to containers |
| **Sufficient Initial Scale** | Supports hundreds of containers across multiple services | Adequate for anticipated initial scale |
| **Service Discovery** | Built-in AWS Cloud Map integration | No additional service discovery infrastructure |

**ECS Capabilities**:
- Task definitions for container specifications
- Service definitions for long-running applications
- Auto-scaling based on CloudWatch metrics
- Blue-green and rolling deployments
- Integration with Application Load Balancer
- CloudWatch Logs integration for centralized logging

**Future Evolution: AWS EKS**

**Kubernetes (EKS) Migration Triggers**:

The system will transition from ECS to EKS when one or more of the following conditions are met:

| Trigger | Threshold | Rationale |
|---------|-----------|-----------|
| **Request Volume** | System sustains > 1,000 requests/second | Kubernetes provides more sophisticated autoscaling and resource optimization |
| **Microservices Complexity** | > 10 independent services | Kubernetes service mesh (Istio, Linkerd) simplifies inter-service communication |
| **Engineering Team Size** | > 10 engineers | Kubernetes ecosystem offers better tooling for larger teams (Helm, Argo CD, Flux) |
| **Advanced Deployment Patterns** | Canary, A/B testing, progressive delivery required | Kubernetes-native tools (Argo Rollouts, Flagger) provide sophisticated deployment strategies |
| **Multi-Cloud Requirements** | Requirement to deploy on non-AWS clouds | Kubernetes provides cloud-agnostic orchestration |
| **Service Mesh Needs** | Complex inter-service communication, mTLS, circuit breakers | Istio/Linkerd provide advanced traffic management on Kubernetes |

**EKS Benefits (Post-Migration)**:
- **Standardized Platform**: Kubernetes skills transferable across cloud providers
- **Rich Ecosystem**: Helm charts, operators, extensive tooling (Argo CD, Prometheus, Grafana)
- **Advanced Scheduling**: More sophisticated resource allocation and bin-packing
- **Service Mesh**: Istio or Linkerd for advanced traffic management, observability
- **GitOps**: Argo CD or Flux for declarative infrastructure management

**Migration Path**:
1. **Phase 1 (Year 1)**: ECS for simplicity and operational efficiency
2. **Phase 2 (Trigger Met)**: Pilot migration of non-critical service to EKS
3. **Phase 3**: Incremental migration of remaining services
4. **Phase 4**: Complete migration, decommission ECS infrastructure

### 8.5.2 Cluster Architecture

**ECS Cluster Configuration** (Initial Deployment):

**Cluster Structure**:

```
ECS Cluster: 6nove4-production
├── Service: api-server
│   ├── Task Definition: api-server:42 (version number)
│   ├── Desired Count: 4-20 (auto-scaling)
│   ├── Launch Type: Fargate (serverless) or EC2
│   ├── Network Mode: awsvpc (dedicated ENI per task)
│   ├── Load Balancer: api-alb (target group: api-server-tg)
│   ├── Auto-Scaling: Target tracking based on CPU/memory/request count
│   └── Health Check: /health endpoint, 30s interval, 3 failure threshold
│
├── Service: background-worker (future expansion)
│   ├── Task Definition: background-worker:latest
│   ├── Desired Count: 2-10
│   ├── Purpose: Async job processing (AI generation, file processing)
│   └── Queue: MongoDB-based job queue
│
└── Shared Resources
    ├── Application Load Balancer (api-alb)
    ├── CloudWatch Log Groups (/ecs/6nove4/production/*)
    ├── IAM Task Roles (ECSTaskExecutionRole, ECSTaskRole)
    └── Security Groups (ALB, application, cache)
```

**ECS Task Definition** (Detailed Configuration):

```json
{
  "family": "api-server",
  "cpu": "2048",
  "memory": "4096",
  "networkMode": "awsvpc",
  "requiresCompatibilities": ["FARGATE"],
  "executionRoleArn": "arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT_ID:role/ECSTaskExecutionRole",
  "taskRoleArn": "arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT_ID:role/ECSTaskRole",
  "containerDefinitions": [
    {
      "name": "flask-api",
      "image": "123456789.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/api-server:1.2.3",
      "cpu": 2048,
      "memory": 4096,
      "portMappings": [
        {
          "containerPort": 5000,
          "protocol": "tcp"
        }
      ],
      "environment": [
        {"name": "ENVIRONMENT", "value": "production"},
        {"name": "LOG_LEVEL", "value": "INFO"},
        {"name": "WORKERS", "value": "4"},
        {"name": "THREADS", "value": "2"}
      ],
      "secrets": [
        {
          "name": "MONGODB_URI",
          "valueFrom": "arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-east-1:ACCOUNT_ID:secret:prod/mongodb-uri"
        },
        {
          "name": "REDIS_URL",
          "valueFrom": "arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-east-1:ACCOUNT_ID:secret:prod/redis-url"
        },
        {
          "name": "AUTH0_CLIENT_SECRET",
          "valueFrom": "arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-east-1:ACCOUNT_ID:secret:prod/auth0-secret"
        },
        {
          "name": "OPENAI_API_KEY",
          "valueFrom": "arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-east-1:ACCOUNT_ID:secret:prod/openai-key"
        }
      ],
      "logConfiguration": {
        "logDriver": "awslogs",
        "options": {
          "awslogs-group": "/ecs/6nove4/production/api-server",
          "awslogs-region": "us-east-1",
          "awslogs-stream-prefix": "ecs",
          "awslogs-datetime-format": "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"
        }
      },
      "healthCheck": {
        "command": ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -f http://localhost:5000/health || exit 1"],
        "interval": 30,
        "timeout": 3,
        "retries": 3,
        "startPeriod": 60
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

**Alternative: EKS Cluster Architecture** (Future State):

**Cluster Configuration**:

```
EKS Cluster: 6nove4-production-eks
├── Control Plane
│   ├── Version: Latest Kubernetes (e.g., 1.28)
│   ├── Endpoint: Private and public access
│   ├── Logging: API server, audit, authenticator, controller manager, scheduler
│   └── Networking: VPC CNI plugin for pod networking
│
├── Node Groups
│   ├── General Purpose: t3.medium instances (2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM)
│   │   ├── Min: 2 nodes, Max: 20 nodes
│   │   ├── Auto-scaling based on pod resource requests
│   │   └── Spot instances for cost optimization (development/staging)
│   └── High Memory (future): r6g.large instances for memory-intensive workloads
│
├── Namespaces
│   ├── production (main application workloads)
│   ├── monitoring (Prometheus, Grafana, alerting)
│   ├── ingress (Nginx Ingress Controller)
│   └── kube-system (Kubernetes system components)
│
└── Deployments
    ├── api-server (4-20 replicas, HorizontalPodAutoscaler)
    ├── background-worker (2-10 replicas)
    └── Supporting services (Redis, monitoring exporters)
```

**Kubernetes Deployment Manifest** (Illustrative):

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api-server
  namespace: production
spec:
  replicas: 4
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api-server
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: api-server
        version: v1.2.3
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: api-server-sa
      containers:
      - name: flask-api
        image: 123456789.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/api-server:1.2.3
        ports:
        - containerPort: 5000
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: 2000m
            memory: 4Gi
          limits:
            cpu: 2000m
            memory: 4Gi
        env:
        - name: ENVIRONMENT
          value: "production"
        - name: LOG_LEVEL
          value: "INFO"
        envFrom:
        - secretRef:
            name: api-server-secrets
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 5000
          initialDelaySeconds: 60
          periodSeconds: 30
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 5000
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
          periodSeconds: 10
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: api-server-svc
  namespace: production
spec:
  selector:
    app: api-server
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 5000
  type: ClusterIP
---
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: api-server-hpa
  namespace: production
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: api-server
  minReplicas: 4
  maxReplicas: 20
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 70
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: memory
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 70
```

### 8.5.3 Service Deployment Strategy

**Primary Strategy: Rolling Update** (Zero-Downtime Deployment)

**ECS Rolling Update Configuration**:

```json
{
  "deploymentConfiguration": {
    "deploymentCircuitBreaker": {
      "enable": true,
      "rollback": true
    },
    "maximumPercent": 200,
    "minimumHealthyPercent": 50
  }
}
```

**Rolling Update Process**:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Dev as Developer
    participant CI as GitHub Actions<br/>CI/CD Pipeline
    participant ECR as Amazon ECR
    participant ECS as ECS Service
    participant ALB as Application<br/>Load Balancer
    participant Old as Old Tasks<br/>(Version 1.2.2)
    participant New as New Tasks<br/>(Version 1.2.3)
    
    Note over Dev,New: Rolling Deployment Process
    
    Dev->>CI: 1. Git push to main branch
    CI->>CI: 2. Run tests + build Docker image
    CI->>ECR: 3. Push image (api-server:1.2.3)
    CI->>ECS: 4. Update task definition<br/>(new image version)
    
    Note over ECS,New: Deployment Phase (5-10 minutes)
    
    ECS->>New: 5. Launch new tasks<br/>(Max 200% = 8 tasks total)
    New->>New: 6. Container startup + health checks<br/>(~60 seconds)
    New->>ALB: 7. Register new tasks<br/>(after 2 successful health checks)
    ALB->>New: 8. Begin routing traffic<br/>(gradual traffic shift)
    
    Note over Old,New: Parallel Operation (2-3 minutes)
    
    ALB->>Old: 9. Traffic to old + new tasks
    ALB->>New: 10. Traffic to old + new tasks
    
    ECS->>Old: 11. Deregister old tasks from ALB<br/>(after new tasks healthy)
    ALB->>Old: 12. Stop new connections<br/>(Connection draining: 30s)
    Old->>Old: 13. Complete in-flight requests
    ECS->>Old: 14. Terminate old tasks<br/>(after draining complete)
    
    Note over ECS,New: Deployment Complete
    
    ECS->>CI: 15. Deployment SUCCESS
    CI->>Dev: 16. Notification (Slack/Email)
    
    alt Deployment Failure
        New->>ECS: Health checks fail (3 consecutive)
        ECS->>ECS: Circuit breaker activated
        ECS->>Old: Rollback to old task definition
        ECS->>CI: Deployment FAILED
        CI->>Dev: Failure notification
    end
```

**Rolling Update Parameters**:

| Parameter | Value | Purpose |
|-----------|-------|---------|
| **minimumHealthyPercent** | 50% | Allow stopping up to 50% of tasks during deployment |
| **maximumPercent** | 200% | Allow doubling task count during deployment (4 → 8 tasks temporarily) |
| **Health Check Grace Period** | 60 seconds | Time for container to start before health checks begin |
| **Health Check Interval** | 30 seconds | ALB checks health every 30 seconds |
| **Healthy Threshold** | 2 consecutive successes | New task must pass 2 health checks before receiving traffic |
| **Unhealthy Threshold** | 3 consecutive failures | Task marked unhealthy after 3 failures (90 seconds) |
| **Connection Draining** | 30 seconds | Time for old tasks to complete in-flight requests |
| **Total Deployment Time** | 5-10 minutes | Complete deployment from start to finish |

**Deployment Circuit Breaker**:

ECS deployment circuit breaker automatically rolls back failed deployments:

**Trigger Conditions**:
- New tasks fail health checks repeatedly
- New tasks crash during startup
- New tasks exceed memory limits

**Behavior**:
1. ECS detects deployment failure (new tasks not reaching healthy state)
2. Circuit breaker stops deployment
3. ECS automatically rolls back to previous task definition
4. Old tasks remain running, no service disruption
5. CloudWatch alarm triggered, engineering team notified

**Alternative Deployment Strategies** (Future Enhancements):

**Blue-Green Deployment**:

**Description**: Deploy complete new environment (green), switch traffic from old (blue) to new, keep old for quick rollback

**Implementation**:
- Create duplicate ECS service with new task definition (green)
- Both services register with separate target groups on same ALB
- Use weighted target groups to gradually shift traffic (0% → 25% → 50% → 100%)
- After validation, terminate blue environment

**Benefits**:
- Instant rollback (switch traffic back to blue)
- Zero downtime
- Full environment testing before cutover

**Trade-offs**:
- Higher cost (temporary double infrastructure)
- More complex orchestration
- Requires infrastructure-as-code automation

**Canary Deployment**:

**Description**: Route small percentage of traffic to new version, gradually increase if metrics acceptable

**Implementation**:
- Deploy new version with 1-2 tasks
- Configure ALB weighted target groups: 90% old, 10% new (canary)
- Monitor metrics (error rate, latency, business KPIs) for canary traffic
- If metrics acceptable, gradually increase canary percentage: 10% → 25% → 50% → 100%
- If metrics degraded, immediately rollback to 100% old version

**Benefits**:
- Limited blast radius (only 10% of users impacted by potential issues)
- Data-driven rollout decisions
- Early issue detection before full rollout

**Requirements**:
- Sophisticated traffic routing (service mesh or advanced ALB configuration)
- Real-time metrics and alerting
- Automated rollout/rollback decisions based on metrics

### 8.5.4 Auto-Scaling Configuration

**ECS Service Auto-Scaling**:

ECS implements auto-scaling through AWS Application Auto Scaling service with multiple scaling policies operating concurrently.

**Scaling Policies**:

**Policy 1: CPU-Based Target Tracking**

```json
{
  "PolicyName": "cpu-target-tracking",
  "PolicyType": "TargetTrackingScaling",
  "TargetTrackingScalingPolicyConfiguration": {
    "TargetValue": 70.0,
    "PredefinedMetricSpecification": {
      "PredefinedMetricType": "ECSServiceAverageCPUUtilization"
    },
    "ScaleOutCooldown": 60,
    "ScaleInCooldown": 300
  }
}
```

**Behavior**:
- **Target**: Maintain 70% average CPU utilization across all tasks
- **Scale-Out**: When CPU > 70% for 2 minutes, add 1 task every 60 seconds until CPU ≤ 70%
- **Scale-In**: When CPU < 30% for 5 minutes, remove 1 task every 300 seconds (conservative)
- **Example**: 4 tasks @ 80% CPU → Add 1 task → 5 tasks @ 64% CPU (balanced)

**Policy 2: Memory-Based Target Tracking**

```json
{
  "PolicyName": "memory-target-tracking",
  "PolicyType": "TargetTrackingScaling",
  "TargetTrackingScalingPolicyConfiguration": {
    "TargetValue": 70.0,
    "PredefinedMetricSpecification": {
      "PredefinedMetricType": "ECSServiceAverageMemoryUtilization"
    },
    "ScaleOutCooldown": 60,
    "ScaleInCooldown": 300
  }
}
```

**Behavior**:
- **Target**: Maintain 70% average memory utilization
- **Rationale**: Memory leaks or memory-intensive operations trigger scaling before OOM (Out Of Memory) errors

**Policy 3: Request-Based Step Scaling** (ALB Request Count)

```json
{
  "PolicyName": "request-count-step-scaling",
  "PolicyType": "StepScaling",
  "StepScalingPolicyConfiguration": {
    "AdjustmentType": "ChangeInCapacity",
    "Cooldown": 60,
    "MetricAggregationType": "Average",
    "StepAdjustments": [
      {
        "MetricIntervalLowerBound": 0,
        "MetricIntervalUpperBound": 50,
        "ScalingAdjustment": 2
      },
      {
        "MetricIntervalLowerBound": 50,
        "MetricIntervalUpperBound": 100,
        "ScalingAdjustment": 4
      },
      {
        "MetricIntervalLowerBound": 100,
        "ScalingAdjustment": 6
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

**CloudWatch Alarm Configuration**:

```json
{
  "AlarmName": "api-server-high-request-count",
  "MetricName": "RequestCountPerTarget",
  "Namespace": "AWS/ApplicationELB",
  "Statistic": "Sum",
  "Period": 60,
  "EvaluationPeriods": 2,
  "Threshold": 500,
  "ComparisonOperator": "GreaterThanThreshold",
  "AlarmActions": ["arn:aws:autoscaling:us-east-1:ACCOUNT_ID:scalingPolicy:..."]
}
```

**Step Scaling Behavior**:

| Request Count/Target | Current Capacity | Scaling Action | New Capacity |
|---------------------|------------------|----------------|--------------|
| **< 500/target** | Any | No action | No change |
| **500-550/target** | 4 tasks | Add 2 tasks | 6 tasks |
| **550-600/target** | 4 tasks | Add 4 tasks | 8 tasks |
| **> 600/target** | 4 tasks | Add 6 tasks | 10 tasks |

**Auto-Scaling Constraints**:

```json
{
  "MinCapacity": 2,
  "MaxCapacity": 20
}
```

| Parameter | Value | Rationale |
|-----------|-------|-----------|
| **MinCapacity** | 2 | High availability requirement (at least 2 tasks across 2 AZs) |
| **MaxCapacity** | 20 | Cost control limit (configurable based on budget) |
| **Scale-Out Cooldown** | 60 seconds | Allow new tasks to start and receive traffic before adding more |
| **Scale-In Cooldown** | 300 seconds (5 minutes) | Conservative scale-in prevents thrashing (scale up/down/up/down) |

**Auto-Scaling Scenarios**:

**Scenario 1: Gradual Traffic Increase**

```
Time    | Requests/Sec | CPU % | Memory % | Task Count | Action
--------|-------------|-------|----------|------------|--------
10:00   | 400         | 50%   | 55%      | 4          | Stable
10:15   | 800         | 75%   | 65%      | 4          | CPU > 70%, add 1 task
10:17   | 800         | 64%   | 60%      | 5          | Stable (CPU balanced)
10:30   | 1,200       | 76%   | 70%      | 5          | CPU > 70%, add 1 task
10:32   | 1,200       | 67%   | 65%      | 6          | Stable
```

**Scenario 2: Sudden Traffic Spike**

```
Time    | Requests/Sec | ALB Target Count | Task Count | Action
--------|-------------|------------------|------------|--------
11:00   | 500         | 125/target       | 4          | Stable
11:01   | 2,500       | 625/target       | 4          | Request count > 600, add 6 tasks (step scaling)
11:03   | 2,500       | 250/target       | 10         | Stable (request count balanced)
```

**Scenario 3: Traffic Decrease (Scale-In)**

```
Time    | CPU % | Memory % | Task Count | Action
--------|-------|----------|------------|--------
14:00   | 35%   | 40%      | 10         | CPU < 40%, wait for 5-minute cooldown
14:05   | 32%   | 38%      | 10         | Cooldown complete, remove 1 task
14:06   | 36%   | 42%      | 9          | Stable
14:11   | 28%   | 35%      | 9          | Remove 1 task
14:12   | 31%   | 39%      | 8          | Stable
```

**Monitoring and Tuning**:

Auto-scaling configuration requires ongoing tuning based on actual load patterns:

**Metrics to Monitor**:
- **Task CPU/Memory Utilization**: Should average 60-80% (target: 70%)
- **Scaling Events**: Frequency and magnitude of scale-out/scale-in events
- **Response Time**: Ensure P95 latency < 500ms during scaling events
- **Task Stability**: Tasks should not crash due to resource exhaustion during high load

**Tuning Actions**:
- **Increase Target CPU/Memory**: If utilization consistently < 50%, increase target to 80% (reduce costs)
- **Decrease Target CPU/Memory**: If P95 latency degrades during high utilization, decrease target to 60% (improve performance)
- **Adjust MaxCapacity**: If frequently hitting max capacity, increase limit (requires budget approval)
- **Adjust Cooldowns**: If thrashing observed, increase cooldown periods

### 8.5.5 Resource Allocation Policies

**Task-Level Resource Allocation**:

Each ECS task receives explicit CPU and memory allocations ensuring predictable performance:

**API Server Task**:

```
CPU: 2 vCPU (2048 CPU units)
Memory: 4 GB (4096 MiB)

Rationale:
- Gunicorn workers: 4 (matches vCPU count for optimal CPU utilization)
- Threads per worker: 2
- Total concurrent requests: 4 workers × 2 threads = 8 concurrent requests per container
- Worker timeout: 30 seconds (prevents hung requests from blocking workers)
```

**Resource Allocation Formula**:

```
Recommended vCPU = Number of Gunicorn Workers
Recommended Memory = (Worker Memory × Workers) + Overhead

Example:
- 4 workers × 800 MB/worker = 3,200 MB
- Python interpreter + libraries overhead: 800 MB
- Total: 4,096 MB (4 GB)
```

**Connection Pool Allocation**:

Database and cache connection pools sized to prevent connection exhaustion:

**MongoDB Connection Pooling**:

```python
# Per Gunicorn worker configuration
mongodb_config = {
    "minPoolSize": 5,
    "maxPoolSize": 10,
    "waitQueueTimeoutMS": 5000,
    "maxIdleTimeMS": 300000,
    "maxLifeTimeMS": 1800000
}

#### Total per container: 4 workers × 10 connections = 40 connections
#### Total per cluster (4 containers): 160 connections
```

**Connection Pool Sizing Considerations**:

| Parameter | Value | Rationale |
|-----------|-------|-----------|
| **minPoolSize** | 5 | Keep connections warm, reduce latency for connection establishment |
| **maxPoolSize** | 10 per worker | Limit total connections, prevent database overload (MongoDB Atlas M30: 1,500 connection limit) |
| **waitQueueTimeoutMS** | 5,000 ms | Fail fast if connection pool exhausted (circuit breaker pattern) |
| **maxIdleTimeMS** | 300,000 ms (5 min) | Close idle connections to free database resources |
| **maxLifeTimeMS** | 1,800,000 ms (30 min) | Rotate connections periodically (credential rotation, DNS updates) |

**Cluster-Wide Connection Budget**:

```
MongoDB Atlas M30: 1,500 connection limit
├── Application Containers (4 typical, 20 max): 160-800 connections
├── Background Workers (2-10): 20-100 connections
├── Reserved for admin/monitoring: 100 connections
└── Safety Buffer: 400+ connections
```

**Redis Connection Pooling**:

```python
# Per Gunicorn worker configuration
redis_config = {
    "max_connections": 5,
    "socket_timeout": 1.0,
    "socket_connect_timeout": 1.0,
    "socket_keepalive": True
}

#### Total per container: 4 workers × 5 connections = 20 connections
#### Total per cluster: 80 connections (well within ElastiCache limits)
```

**Resource Monitoring**:

CloudWatch metrics track resource utilization for optimization:

| Metric | Target | Alert Threshold | Action |
|--------|--------|-----------------|--------|
| **Container CPU** | 60-80% average | > 85% sustained (10 min) | Investigate CPU-intensive operations, consider vertical scaling |
| **Container Memory** | 60-75% average | > 85% sustained (5 min) | Check for memory leaks, consider increasing memory allocation |
| **MongoDB Connections** | 160-800 active | > 1,200 (80% of limit) | Scale containers, optimize connection pooling |
| **Redis Connections** | 80-400 active | > 10,000 (approaching ElastiCache limit) | Investigate connection leaks, validate connection pooling |
| **Request Queue Time** | < 100ms | > 500ms | Indicates resource contention, scale containers |
| **Worker Timeout Errors** | 0 | > 1% of requests | Indicates long-running requests, optimize application code or increase worker timeout |

## 8.6 CI/CD PIPELINE

### 8.6.1 Build Pipeline

#### 8.6.1.1 Source Control Triggers

**Source Control Platform**: **GitHub**

**Trigger Events**:

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main         # Staging deployment
      - develop      # Development deployment
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main         # PR validation
      - develop      # PR validation
  workflow_dispatch:  # Manual trigger
```

**Branching Strategy**:

| Branch | Purpose | Deployment Target | Automatic Deploy |
|--------|---------|-------------------|------------------|
| **feature/*** | Feature development | None (local dev only) | No |
| **develop** | Integration branch | Development environment | Yes (on merge) |
| **main** | Stable release candidate | Staging environment | Yes (on merge) |
| **production** | Production release | Production environment | No (manual approval required) |

**Pull Request Workflow**:

1. Developer creates feature branch from `develop`
2. Developer pushes commits to feature branch (no deployment)
3. Developer opens pull request to `develop` or `main`
4. CI pipeline triggered:
   - Run linting (flake8, mypy, black for Python; ESLint, Prettier for TypeScript)
   - Run unit tests with coverage reporting
   - Run integration tests
   - Build Docker image (validate Dockerfile, don't push)
   - Security scan (dependency vulnerabilities, SAST)
5. Status checks pass/fail visible in GitHub PR
6. Reviewer approves PR
7. Developer merges to `develop` or `main`
8. Post-merge deployment pipeline triggered

#### 8.6.1.2 Build Environment Requirements

**Backend Build Pipeline (Python/Flask)**:

```yaml
name: Backend CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, develop]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    strategy:
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.11"]
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v3
      
      - name: Set up Python ${{ matrix.python-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
          cache: 'pip'
      
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r requirements.txt
          pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
      
      - name: Run linting (flake8)
        run: |
          flake8 src/ --count --show-source --statistics
      
      - name: Run type checking (mypy)
        run: |
          mypy src/ --strict
      
      - name: Run code formatting check (black)
        run: |
          black --check src/
      
      - name: Run unit tests
        run: |
          pytest tests/ \
            --cov=src \
            --cov-report=xml \
            --cov-report=html \
            --junitxml=test-results.xml
      
      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v3
        with:
          file: ./coverage.xml
          flags: backend
          name: backend-coverage
      
      - name: Upload test results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        with:
          name: test-results
          path: test-results.xml
```

**Frontend Build Pipeline (TypeScript/React)**:

```yaml
name: Frontend CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, develop]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    strategy:
      matrix:
        node-version: ["20.x"]
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v3
      
      - name: Set up Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
          cache: 'npm'
      
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci --prefer-offline
      
      - name: Run linting (ESLint)
        run: npm run lint
      
      - name: Run type checking (TypeScript)
        run: npx tsc --noEmit
      
      - name: Run unit tests
        run: npm test -- --coverage --watchAll=false
      
      - name: Build application
        run: npm run build
      
      - name: Upload build artifacts
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        with:
          name: frontend-build
          path: dist/
```
